subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh and manage followed publishers

question: Should OpenClaw core own the signed publisher-feed trust, SQLite persistence, scheduler, CLI, and Gateway RPC control plane, or should this remain a plugin/ClawHub capability behind existing extension seams?
rationale: The submitted implementation creates a broad, durable core product and security boundary; repository policy prefers optional marketplace and service workflows outside core unless maintainers explicitly establish a missing generic core API.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Keep publisher-feed fetching, trust configuration, persistence, and operator workflow in an external package unless a concrete missing core seam is identified.

options.title: Sponsor a minimal core seam
options.body: Approve only the generic capability needed in core, with publisher-specific trust, scheduler, storage, and commands owned by a plugin and documented upgrade contract.

options.title: Approve the full core surface
options.body: Accept this as a supported core feature and require explicit API, storage, security, and upgrade documentation before merge.

recommendation.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
recommendation.body: Keep publisher-feed fetching, trust configuration, persistence, and operator workflow in an external package unless a concrete missing core seam is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the consolidated feature stack and can supply the boundary rationale and proof, while the final product decision remains with repository owners.
